post.description: To see which partners AlphaFold DB predicts a protein binds and how confident each interface is. These are predictions from a selective dataset (AlphaFold DB shows NVIDIA complexes only above its own pDockQ2 and ipSAE cut-offs), so a missing partner is not evidence of no interaction, and partners can come from other species: check each partner's organism.

gene.description: Gene symbol (TP53, CD52, HLA-A), resolved to the one reviewed (Swiss-Prot) UniProt entry with that gene name, or that synonym, in organism. A symbol shared by several entries is invalid_input listing them.

id.description: UniProt accession (P04637), isoform (P04637-2), entry name (P53_HUMAN), AlphaFold DB model ID (AF-P04637-F1, AF-0000000000710001) or alphafold.ebi.ac.uk entry URL; case-insensitive. Exactly one of id and gene.

limit.description:
Most complexes to return, highest ipTM first.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 25.

min_iptm.description:
Only complexes with ipTM at least this (0.8 keeps confident interfaces).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 1.

organism.description: Organism for gene: NCBI taxonomy ID (9606) or name (human, Mus musculus). Default 9606 (human). Only with gene.

200.description:
Predicted protein complexes in AlphaFold DB that contain a protein, by UniProt accession, entry name, model ID, entry URL or gene symbol and organism; or one complex by its model ID (AF-0000000065932364). Each complex lists its partners (UniProt accession, gene, protein name, organism, copies), assembly, the provider dataset (mostly NVIDIA's proteome-scale homo- and heterodimers), mean pLDDT, the interface scores ipTM, ipSAE, pDockQ, pDockQ2 and LIS, interface_confidence from ipTM (high 0.8 or more, medium 0.6 to 0.8, low under 0.6), links to the mmCIF and PAE image, and its entry page. Sorted by ipTM, highest first; min_iptm filters and limit caps the list. A protein with no predicted complexes returns an empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `complexes` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assembly` | string | homomer or heteromer. |
| `files` | object |  |
| `interface_confidence` | string | From ipTM: high >= 0.8 (confident interface), medium 0.6-0.8 (grey zone), low < 0.6 (likely wrong). |
| `ipsae` | number | Interface score ipSAE, 0 to 1. |
| `iptm` | number | Interface predicted TM-score, 0 to 1. |
| `lis` | number | Local interaction score, 0 to 1. |
| `mean_plddt` | number |  |
| `model_id` | string | AlphaFold DB complex model ID. |
| `name` | string | AlphaFold DB's complex name. |
| `oligomeric_state` | string | e.g. dimer. |
| `partners` | object[] | Chains in the complex with copy numbers; partners can be from another species. |
| `pdockq` | number | pDockQ, 0 to 1. |
| `pdockq2` | number | pDockQ2, 0 to 1. |
| `provider` | string | Dataset that predicted it, e.g. NVIDIA. |
| `source_url` | string | AlphaFold DB entry page. |
| `version` | number |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
The AlphaFold DB predicted structure of one protein, by UniProt accession (P04637), isoform (P04637-2), entry name (P53_HUMAN), AlphaFold model ID (AF-P04637-F1, AF-0000000000710001), alphafold.ebi.ac.uk entry URL, or gene symbol and organism. Returns the model ID, version, date, method and provider, the UniProt residue range it covers, mean pLDDT and the share of residues per confidence band with a one-line reading, confident_regions (pLDDT 70 or more) and disordered_regions (pLDDT under 50) as UniProt residue ranges, whether AlphaMissense data exists, and links to the mmCIF, BinaryCIF, PDB, PAE and per-residue confidence files (coordinates are linked, never returned). Isoform and alternative models of the entry are listed in other_models. Merged UniProt accessions are followed. Unknown or deleted accessions and proteins AlphaFold DB does not model (it covers 16 to 2,700 residues) are not_found with the reason.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `model` | object | The model the call is about. Null when AlphaFold DB has no model of the requested sequence but has models of its isoforms (see no_model_reason). |
| `no_model_reason` | string | Why model is null; null otherwise. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `organism` | object |  |
| `other_models` | object[] | Other single-chain models returned for the same request: isoforms of a canonical accession and alternative predictions, with their mean pLDDT. Call prediction with a model_id for its regions. |
| `protein_name` | string | UniProt recommended protein name. |
| `reference_proteome` | boolean | Whether the entry is in a UniProt reference proteome. |
| `requested` | string | The id or gene as given. |
| `resolved_via` | string | How the input became a UniProt accession: null when used as given; uniprot_entry_name or uniprot_merged_accession through UniProt; gene_symbol or gene_synonym when gene matched a primary gene name or a synonym. |
| `reviewed` | boolean | Whether the UniProt entry is reviewed (Swiss-Prot). |
| `source_url` | string | AlphaFold DB entry page of the model. |

200.description:
AlphaMissense pathogenicity predictions (Google DeepMind) for a human protein, from AlphaFold DB: every possible amino-acid substitution scored 0 to 1 and classed likely benign (under 0.34), ambiguous, or likely pathogenic (over 0.564). Pass variants (R175H, p.Arg175His; up to 50) for their scores and classes, checked against the UniProt canonical sequence. Every call also returns a protein summary: class fractions, mean score and sensitive_regions, the residue ranges whose mean score is above 0.564. Takes the same identifiers as prediction. Canonical human sequences only: other organisms and isoforms are not_found. These are research predictions, not clinical classifications.

The response contains the tool result directly.

post.description: Backtests and price history, e.g. 1-minute BTC-USD candles between two dates: call with `granularity: 60`, `start`, `end`, `max_candles: 3000`, then follow `next_start` until it is null.

end.description: Inclusive range end, same forms as `start`. Defaults to now.

granularity.description:
Bucket length in seconds: 60, 300, 900, 3600, 21600 or 86400.

Provider reference: allowed values ["60", "300", "900", "3600", "21600", "86400"]; default 60.

max_candles.description:
Upper bound on buckets fetched in this call (300 per upstream request; requests are made sequentially to respect the 10 req/s public limit).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 3000; default 300.

product_id.description: Trading pair id `BASE-QUOTE` as listed by `list_products`, e.g. `BTC-USD`, `USELESS-USD`. Case-insensitive; the canonical upper-case id is returned. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,20}-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,20}$.

start.description: Inclusive range start: RFC 3339 (`2026-07-24T00:00:00Z`) or a date (`2026-07-24`, midnight UTC). Defaults to `end` minus `max_candles` buckets.

200.description:
Historical OHLCV candles for one trading pair (`GET /products/{product_id}/candles`) at 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h or 1d granularity, oldest first. The exchange serves at most 300 buckets per request, so a wider `start`..`end` range is walked in consecutive 300-bucket windows, up to `max_candles` (default 300, max 3000 = 10 upstream requests) per call; `next_start` continues where the call stopped. Buckets without trades are omitted by the exchange (thin markets return fewer rows than the window length; a `sparse_buckets` warning says so). Values are numbers as the exchange sends them.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `candles` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | number |  |
| `high` | number |  |
| `low` | number |  |
| `open` | number |  |
| `time` | number | Bucket start, Unix seconds, aligned to the granularity. |
| `time_iso` | string | Bucket start, RFC 3339 UTC (derived from `time`). |
| `volume` | number | Base-currency volume traded in the bucket. |

post.description: Start here to find a model slug (e.g. `claude-fable-5-1-high`) for get_model or list_model_providers, to rank models by intelligence, price or speed, or with `slug` to fetch one known model/effort row (legacy slugs included) without paging the whole table.

cursor.description: Opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pattern: ^[0-9]+$.

include_deprecated.description: Include models the site marks deprecated. Since 2026-10-17 the leaderboard page serves only current models, so deprecated rows are usually absent and the result is reported as partial coverage. Implied true when `slug` is given.

limit.description:
Results per page (1-100).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

query.description: Case-insensitive terms matched against model name, short name, slug and creator; every whitespace-separated term must match (substring: `deepseek-v3` also matches `deepseek-v3-0324`; use `slug` for an exact row). Punctuation is folded on both sides, so `Claude Sonnet 5.5`, `claude-sonnet-5.5` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` find the same rows. One model per call: a list of several names matches nothing.

slug.description: Exact model slug at one reasoning effort (e.g. `claude-fable-5-1-high`, `deepseek-v3`) or a pasted https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/{slug} URL: returns that one row (effort siblings such as `-high`/`-low` are not matched). Implies `include_deprecated: true`; a deprecated slug matches only while the page lists deprecated rows (use get_model for it otherwise). Combines with the other filters. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9./:_-]+$.

200.description:
Search the Artificial Analysis LLM leaderboard: every current model and reasoning-effort variant with its Intelligence Index, Intelligence Index cost per task (USD, null when unmeasured), benchmark scores, list prices (USD per 1M tokens: the model's list price as the leaderboard states it, not scoped to an API provider; provider-scoped input, output and cache rates are in list_model_providers and search_provider_endpoints), output speed and latency percentiles, sorted by Intelligence Index; reports the index version the page states. Looks up one row by exact `slug`, or filters by text, creator, reasoning and open-weights status; client-side pages over the whole table.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `benchmarks` | object | Benchmark scores as the site reports them (raw values, not percentages). A key is present only when that surface reports the evaluation; null means the site has not measured it for this model. |
| `context_window_tokens` | number |  |
| `creator_name` | string | Model creator as labelled by the site (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI). |
| `deprecated` | boolean |  |
| `intelligence_index` | number | Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (0..100); null when not evaluated. |
| `intelligence_index_cost_per_task_usd` | number | USD to run one Intelligence Index task, weighted across the index's evaluations at the model's list prices (the leaderboard's Cost per Task column); null when the site has not measured it (unevaluated or estimated index). |
| `intelligence_index_is_estimated` | boolean | True when the site estimates the index from a subset of evaluations. |
| `is_open_weights` | boolean |  |
| `is_reasoning` | boolean |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `performance` | object | Leaderboard performance columns measured by Artificial Analysis; null when the site lists the endpoint (pricing, features) but has not benchmarked it yet. |
| `price_class` | string | Site price class (low, medium, high, ...). |
| `pricing_usd_per_1m_tokens` | object | List prices in USD per 1M tokens as published by the provider and recorded by the site. Blended prices are present only where the site publishes them (model records and per-model provider endpoints). |
| `short_name` | string |  |
| `size_class` | string | Site parameter class (small, medium, large, ...). |
| `slug` | string | Model slug at one reasoning effort, the `/models/{slug}` path segment; input for get_model and list_model_providers. |
| `url` | string | Model page on artificialanalysis.ai. |

| `currency` | string | Currency of every price: EUR. |

| `ean` | string | EAN/GTIN-13; null when the page lists none. |
| `image_url` | string |  |

| `manufacturer_part_number` | string | Manufacturer part number (`Fabrikantcode`); null when the page lists none. |

| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix epoch milliseconds when the page was read. |

200.description:
Keyword search over the Azerty.nl catalogue, one page of up to 24 products in the site's relevance order: article number, name, short spec line, EUR price (incl. and excl. VAT), delivery-time text and product URL. Some keywords redirect to a category page (`landing: listing`) and an exact article number or EAN to its product page (`landing: product`); both are reported as results. Listing cards carry no ratings; use `product` for those.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | number |  |
| `country` | string | Market of the storefront: NL. |
| `currency` | string | Currency of every price: EUR. |
| `has_more` | boolean |  |
| `items` | object[] |  |
| `landing` | string | Which page answered: `search` the result list; `listing` a category or brand page the site's search redirects some keywords to (e.g. `ssd`); `product` the product page an exact article number or EAN redirects to. |
| `language` | string | Storefront language: nl. |
| `next_page` | number | Next page number, null on the last page. |
| `next_page_input` | object | Input for the next page of this search; null on the last page. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix epoch milliseconds when the page was read. |
| `page` | number |  |
| `page_size` | number | Products per page: 24. |
| `query` | string | Normalized query (whitespace collapsed). |

Find blog.google posts by words in their title, summary, URL, topics or author names inside a publication window. The site's own search page is disallowed by robots.txt, so this scans the listing API newest first (up to 10 pages of 50 posts per call, bounded by `since`/`until` and optionally a section, author page or edition) and keeps posts matching every word of `q` (case ignored). post.description: Discover NCT numbers for a topic before calling study or study_dates; list trials by sponsor, status or location.

advanced_filter.description: Essie filter expression applied after the query (filter.advanced), e.g. AREA[StartDateType]ESTIMATED.

agg_filters.description: Facet filters as the site encodes them (aggFilters), e.g. "phase:3,status:rec". Pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]+:[a-zA-Z0-9_ ]+(,[a-zA-Z]+:[a-zA-Z0-9_ ]+)*$.

condition.description: Condition or disease (query.cond), e.g. "Breast Cancer". Essie syntax allowed.

location.description: Location terms: city, state, country or facility (query.locn), e.g. "Boston".

near.description: Only studies with a site within the radius of the coordinate (filter.geo=distance(lat,lon,radius)).

page_size.description:
Studies per page (the API accepts up to 1000; capped at 100 here).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 10.

page_token.description: next_page_token from the previous page. Send the same query parameters again. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$.

sort.description: Sort by a field piece with optional direction, e.g. "LastUpdatePostDate:desc", or "@relevance" (default when a query is given). Pattern: ^(@relevance|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(:(asc|desc))?)$.

status.description: Overall status filter (filter.overallStatus); any of the listed values matches.

term.description: Other terms searched across the record (query.term). Accepts Essie expressions such as AREA[StartDate]RANGE[2025-01-01,MAX].

title.description: Words in the brief or official title, or acronym (query.titles).

DECISION AND ORDER DENYING PETITIONER'S MOTION TO VACATE, SET ASIDE OR CORRECT SENTENCE PURSUANT TO 28 U.S.C. § 2255: Pierre-Louis's motion for relief pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 2255 is denied; no hearing is necessary. See Chang v. United States, 250 F.3d 79, 86 (2d Cir. 2001) (in claims of ineffective assistance, affirming district court's decision to forego a full testimonial hearing where the court "reasonably decided that the testimony of [the defendant] and his trial counsel would add little or nothing to the written submissions"). Furthermore, Pierre-Louis has not made a substantial showing of a denial of a federal right, so no certificate of appealability shall issue. See, e.g., Hamilton v. Superintendent, 2017 WL 1944114, at *6 (S.D.N.Y. 2017) (declining to issue a Certificate of Appealability "because Petitioner has failed to identify a claim that jurists ofreason would find debatable as to whether Petitioner was denied such a right) (citing Slack v. McDaniel, 529 U.S. 473,478 (2000)); Prousalis v. United States, 2018 WL 3471811, at *5 (DLC) (S.D.N.Y. 2018) (citing Hojjl.er v. Bezio, 726 F.3d 144, 154 (2d Cir. 2013); Tankleffv. Senkowski, 135 F.3d 235,241 (2d Cir. 1998); Rodriquez v. Scully, 905 F.2d 24, 24 (2d Cir. 1990)). The Court finds that any appeal by Pierre-Louis from its Order would not be taken in good faith, pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1915(a)(3). Id. (citing Coppedge v. United States, 369 U.S. 438,445 (1962)). This constitutes the decision and order of the Court. (Signed by Judge Colleen McMahon on 4/21/2022) (kv) (Entered: 04/21/2022)

attributes.value: This indicator is related to the national accounts, which are critical for understanding and managing a country's economy. They provide a framework for the analysis of economic performance. National accounts are the basis for estimating the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Gross National Income (GNI), which are the most widely used indicator of economic performance. They are essential for government policymakers, providing the data needed to design and assess fiscal and monetary policies; and are also used by businesses and investors to assess the economic climate and make investment decisions. NAS enable comparison between economies, which is crucial for international trade, investment decisions, and economic competitiveness. More specifically, this indicator is related to national accounts aggregates. Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Income (GNI), and other aggregates provide a snapshot of the size and health of an economy by measuring the total economic activity within a country. They can thus be used by policymakers to design and implement economic policies, as they reflect the overall economic performance and can indicate the need for intervention in certain areas. Aggregates also allow for comparisons between different economies, which can be useful for trade negotiations, investment decisions, and economic benchmarking. By examining aggregates over time, economists and analysts can identify trends, cycles, and potential areas of concern within an economy, and investors can use national accounts aggregates to assess the potential risks and returns of investing in a particular country. Overall, national accounts aggregates are fundamental tools for economic analysis, policy formulation, and decision-making at both the national and international levels.

Gross domestic product (GDP), though widely tracked, may not always be the most relevant summary of aggregated economic performance for all economies, especially when production occurs at the expense of consuming capital stock.









While GDP estimates based on the production approach are generally more reliable than estimates compiled from the income or expenditure side, different countries use different definitions, methods, and reporting standards. World Bank staff review the quality of national accounts data and sometimes make adjustments to improve consistency with international guidelines. Nevertheless, significant discrepancies remain between international standards and actual practice. Many statistical offices, especially those in developing countries, face severe limitations in the resources, time, training, and budgets required to produce reliable and comprehensive series of national accounts statistics.









Among the difficulties faced by compilers of national accounts is the extent of unreported economic activity in the informal or secondary economy. In developing countries a large share of agricultural output is either not exchanged (because it is consumed within the household) or not exchanged for money.

Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

Methodology: National accounts are compiled in accordance with international standards: System of National Accounts, 2008 or 1993 versions. Specific information on how countries compile their national accounts can be found on the IMF website: https://dsbb.imf.org/
Statistical concept(s): The conceptual elements of the SNA (System of National Accounts) measure what takes place in the economy, between which agents, and for what purpose. At the heart of the SNA is the production of goods and services. These may be used for consumption in the period to which the accounts relate or may be accumulated for use in a later period. In simple terms, the amount of value added generated by production represents GDP. The income corresponding to GDP is distributed to the various agents or groups of agents as income and it is the process of distributing and redistributing income that allows one agent to consume the goods and services produced by another agent or to acquire goods and services for later consumption. The way in which the SNA captures this pattern of economic flows is to identify the activities concerned by recognizing the institutional units in the economy and by specifying the structure of accounts capturing the transactions relevant to one stage or another of the process by which goods and services are produced and ultimately consumed.

usage_notes: Always include a non-empty top-level prompt, including when using multi_prompt. Keep it within 2,500 characters; longer prompts are truncated.
For custom shots, set multi_shots to true and provide 1–6 multi_prompt objects. Each object needs prompt (at most 512 characters) and duration (a positive integer from 1 to 15 seconds).
Custom-shot durations are summed for generation and billing; the top-level duration does not override that sum. With multi_shots enabled and no custom shots, the top-level duration is retained.
Native audio uses sound: on or off and defaults to on.
elements contains Kling element IDs as decimal strings. Each ID must belong to the account making the request; arbitrary provider IDs are rejected.

value.content:
## Delivery and retries

* Return any `2xx` response after durably recording the event.
* Network failures and `5xx` responses are retried for up to two hours.
* `4xx` responses are treated as permanent and are not retried.
* Duplicate deliveries are possible. Deduplicate by `request_id` and terminal `status`.
* If delivery fails permanently, retrieve the result through the authenticated status endpoint.

Reject request bodies that do not match the documented envelope, but acknowledge valid duplicate deliveries with `2xx`.
value.description: Receive terminal generation results without continuous polling.

guidance: Start at https://console.higgsfield.ai to discover models and open their model-specific API documentation.
Use the selected model’s documentation for its endpoint, request schema, supported parameters, and examples. Follow its model-specific `llms.txt` link when available.
Use https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/llms.txt for shared authentication, SDK, polling, webhook, and error-handling guidance.
Treat `/docs/openapi.json` as supplementary reference, not the authoritative model catalog. A model’s absence from that file does not establish that it is unavailable.
Check whether model documentation targets production or preview. Do not silently substitute environments, endpoints, or models.
If sources conflict or access prevents verification, describe the specific uncertainty. Distinguish documented availability from access verified with the user’s account.

results.snippet:
## Retry after an ambiguous failure

1. Create the key before sending the generation request.
2. Store the key with your local operation or job record.
3. After a network error, timeout, or `5xx`, retry the same endpoint and parameters with the same key.
4. Store the returned `request_id` and use it
results.title: Retry after an ambiguous failure

results.snippet:
## Safe retry policy

* Retry `GET` status requests after network failures and `5xx` responses.
* Do not retry authentication or validation failures without changing the request.
* Use exponential backoff with jitter.
* Set maximum attempts and a total retry deadline.
* Send an [`Idempotency-Key`](/

200.description:
Full listing of one OpenFEMA dataset version (collection contract `records/list`): pages of `$orderby=id&$top=<page_size>&$skip=<n>`, 1 to 5,000 rows a page (1,000 default; 1,000 declaration rows are 0.9 MB, 1,000 NFIP rows 2.4 MB). Every page re-runs the status query and compares the live `publication_id` with the one pinned in the cursor; when the dataset was refreshed in between the call fails with `invalid_input` code `publication_changed` and the listing restarts, so two publications are never mixed. Records are OpenFEMA's rows as sent (every field; declarations carry femaDeclarationString, disasterNumber, declarationType, declarationDate, incidentType, designatedArea, fipsStateCode, fipsCountyCode, placeCode, the four program flags, lastRefresh, hash, id; NFIP claims dateOfLoss, yearOfLoss, causeOfDamage, floodEvent, ratedFloodZone, waterDepth, the paid amounts, state, countyCode, censusGeoid, latitude, longitude, id) plus `source_record_id` (`<dataset>:v<version>:<id>`), `source_url`, `publication_id` and `retrieved_at`. Segment key for datasets over ~500k rows: `segment_field`/`segment_value` (an equality, e.g. `state` = `TX` for NfipClaims v3: 394k rows) and `year_field`/`year` (one calendar year of a date field, e.g. `dateOfLoss` 2017 with `state` = `TX` for NfipClaims v3). Datasets over 20M rows (NfipPolicies v3: 74.7M) are refused with `invalid_input` code `hand_off`: OpenFEMA cannot serve an ordered page of them within the timeout, so take the parquet/csv files `source_status` lists. `$count=true` is sent on the first page only. A frozen deprecated dataset (rows empty, count positive) is `upstream_error` naming the successor.

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
The complete Canadian Nutrient File record of one food by `food_code` (or a pasted CNF serving-portion / nutrientReport page URL): description, every nutrient the CNF reports for it per 100 g edible portion, joined with the CNF nutrient dictionary (symbol, INFOODS tagname, unit such as g / mg / µg / IU / kcal, decimals, nutrient group) and the data-source code list (provenance; source 1 marks values changed to meet Canadian fortification regulations), plus the food's serving measures with conversion factors and gram weights, refuse (inedible portion) rows and yield rows. Seven to eight anonymous GET calls to /api/canadian-nutrient-file/ (food, nutrientamount, servingsize, refuseamount, yieldamount, nutrientname, nutrientgroup, nutrientsource). An unknown food code is `not_found` (the API answers an empty list).

The response contains the tool result directly.

Find Canadian Nutrient File foods by name. The CNF API has no server-side search: the function downloads the complete food list (GET /api/canadian-nutrient-file/food/, 5,690 rows, ~470 KB) and matches client-side the way the CNF web app does: case- and accent-insensitive, every word of the query must appear somewhere in the food description, in any order ('apple raw' finds 'Pineapple, raw'). A query that is only digits also matches the food code exactly. Results keep the API's order, are paged with `limit`/`offset` and report `total_matches`; no match is a valid empty result. Each row carries the `food_code` that `get_food` takes and the food's CNF serving-size page URL. `lang` selects English or French descriptions (same food codes).

value.description:
•Understand why context is a dynamic, situational capability rather than a static repository of enterprise data
•Learn why semantic models, ontologies and conformed business metrics are critical for reliable AI reasoning
•Explore how organizations can capture undocumented processes and institutional knowledge to reduce agent drift
•Discover how context engineering helps improve AI reliability, governance and business value



While enterprise AI investments continue to surge, most organizations struggle to derive significant business value from GenAI deployments due to inconsistent outputs, unpredictable agent behavior, and runaway token costs. These failures rarely stem from foundation model limitations, but rather from the lack of the contextual information needed to consistently apply organizational knowledge, policies and business logic.




In this webinar, we focus on bridging this operational gap by getting fully grounded in the core principles of context layers. Rather than relying on surface-level prompting, we will demystify what makes up an enterprise context layer, why it serves as the essential control plane for agentic systems, and how it connects static data to dynamic AI execution. Attendees will gain a clear, practical understanding of how a well-structured context layer supports higher quality reasoning and turns stateless models into trusted business assets.




Return to this web page to watch the webinar. Contact us at gartnerwebinars@gartner.com with questions about viewing this webinar.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page of the same search. Pass it with the same keyword, location and filters.

easy_apply_only.description: Only jobs that take Glassdoor's Easy Apply (applicationType=1).

employer_id.description:
Only jobs from this Glassdoor employer id (companyId; id from suggest_employers, e.g. 9079 for Google).

Provider reference: minimum 1.

employer_size.description:
Employer size band (employerSizes): 1 = 1-50, 2 = 51-200, 3 = 201-500, 4 = 501-1000, 5 = 1001+ employees.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5.

industry_id.description:
Glassdoor industry id (industryNId) as listed in the site's industry filter.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

keyword.description: Job title or keywords, e.g. "data analyst" or "registered nurse" (the site's sc.keyword). Must contain a letter or digit.

location_id.description:
Glassdoor location id (location_id from suggest_locations, e.g. 1132348 for New York, NY; 428 for New York State; 1 for the United States). Omit to search the whole United States.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

location_type.description:
Kind of location_id as Glassdoor codes it (location_type from suggest_locations): C city, S state, N country. Default C.

Provider reference: allowed values ["C", "S", "N"]; default "C".

min_rating.description:
Minimum employer overall rating, 1 to 4 stars (minRating).

Provider reference: allowed values ["1", "2", "3", "4"].

min_salary.description:
Annual pay floor in USD (minSalary); the site's UI steps are 40000 to 180000 by 20000, other values are passed through as given.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000000.

posted_within_days.description:
Only jobs posted within the last N days (the site's fromAge filter; its UI offers 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30).

Provider reference: allowed values ["1", "3", "7", "14", "30"].

radius_miles.description:
Search radius around a city location in miles (radius). The site's default is 50 for a city; 0 means the exact location only.

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "5", "10", "15", "25", "50", "100"].

seniority.description:
Seniority level (seniorityType).

Provider reference: allowed values ["internship", "entrylevel", "midseniorlevel", "director", "executive"].

sort.description:
Result order: the site's relevance (default), newest first (date_desc) or oldest first (date_asc).

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "date_desc", "date_asc"].

value.description_html:
Discord is a voice, video and text platform that helps friends come together to hang out, play games and have fun. When Jason Citron and Stanislav Vishnevskiy founded Discord in 2015 they had a hunch that multiplayer gaming would be the future of entertainment and that people would need a communications platform designed for them to talk with their gaming friends. Today, gaming has become the largest form of entertainment in the world, bigger than movies and music combined. It’s the fastest-growing as well.

 

Discord makes it feel like you’re playing in the same room with friends. Discord users can communicate through 1:1 direct messages (DMs), group direct messages (GDMs) and Servers where friends can easily gather in voice, text and video chats before, during and after gaming. High quality streaming and a seamless experience across devices lets people play and interact together as if they were in person. Almost all activity on Discord happens in small, private friend spaces.

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to talk and hang out before, during, and after playing games.

So if this strikes a chord, come join us in our mission! Explore our latest job listings and apply today!

value.content_html:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Creators are people who build audiences across the internet: influential voices whose communities listen to them and want to spend time together. Many of those communities already live on Discord, but our relationship with creators has grown organically. We have an opportunity to listen more closely, serve them more intentionally, and build a relationship that reflects the role they play on our platform.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Program Manager to build Discord’s approach to creators from the ground up. You’ll begin with a selected group of creators already using Discord, build the fundamentals that serve them well, and develop programs that make their experience on Discord better. Over time, you’ll turn what works into programs that can serve creators at scale and, eventually, give new creators more reasons to choose Discord. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can lead through judgment, relationships, and execution. You’ll report to the Director of Marketing, Player Communications and partner closely with Support, Product, Marketing, Communications, Partnerships, Policy, and more.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build Discord’s creator strategy from the bottom up, starting with direct conversations and a clear understanding of what creators already on Discord need from us.
  • Bring together the creator work that exists across Discord today, establish clear ownership, and turn a collection of early efforts into a coherent program.
  • Define who we mean by creators and develop an initial approach for selecting and serving a trusted group across games, platforms, formats, and communities.
  • Create more than one program for creators, beginning with the fundamentals: accelerated support, clear paths for escalation, and reliable channels for two-way communication.
  • Manage relationships with important creators directly. Understand how they use Discord, help them solve meaningful problems, and build trust by following through.
  • Build a creator council or network that gives us a consistent view of what creators are seeing, where Discord is falling short, and what would make the platform more useful to them and their communities.
  • Build systems and playbooks that let a selected program grow over time without losing the relationships and responsiveness that made it valuable.

What you should have

  • A strong passion for Discord and/or gaming, and an appreciation for the creators and communities we serve.
  • 7+ years in creator partnerships, community, platform programs, marketing, product partnerships, or a related field.
  • Deeply familiar with how creators build audiences, operate their businesses, and manage communities across platforms like YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram, Patreon, Reddit, and Discord.
  • You have built and operated creator or partner programs at scale, and you understand how to begin with a selected group without designing something that can never grow beyond it.
  • Biased to ship and iterate. You can launch a useful first version, learn from it, and raise the ambition over time.
  • Comfortable leading as an individual contributor. You create alignment and momentum across teams without relying on headcount or reporting lines.
  • An excellent cross-functional partner across Support, Product, Marketing, Comms, Partnerships, Policy, and more.

Bonus Points

  • You have built a creator, partner, ambassador, advisory, or VIP program for a consumer platform.
  • You have designed accelerated support or escalation programs for influential users.
  • You have worked directly with gaming creators and understand the relationship between creators, games, and communities.
  • You have built programs involving product access, creator events, recognition, or discovery.
  • You have helped turn creator feedback into product changes, policies, or platform strategy.
  • You have built a program that began with a small trusted group and expanded without losing what made it valuable.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $256,000 to $288,000 + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity, or benefits.

Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma counties). Relocation assistance may be available. 

Why Discord? 

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We're a multiplatform, multigenerational and multiplayer platform that helps people deepen their friendships around games and shared interests, and helps developers build and grow their businesses. We believe games give us a way to have fun with our favorite people, whether listening to music together or grinding in competitive matches for diamond rank. Join us in our mission! Your future is just a click away!

Discord is committed to inclusion and providing reasonable accommodations during the interview process. We want you to feel set up for success, so if you are in need of reasonable accommodations, please let your recruiter know.

Please see our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy for details regarding Discord’s collection and usage of personal information relating to the application and recruitment process by clicking HERE.

# Grafana Docker image

## Run the Grafana Docker container

Start the Docker container by binding Grafana to external port `3000`.

```bash
docker run -d --name=grafana -p 3000:3000 grafana/grafana
```

Try it out, default admin user credentials are admin/admin.

Further documentation on how to run Docker can be found at http://docs.grafana.org/installation/docker/.

## Changelog

You can find information about Grafana in our [docs](https://grafana.com/docs/), or find out what's new in the latest release [here](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/whatsnew/)!

post.description: Browse or filter equipment for sale by category or make; discover filter values via `include_facets`; paginate with `continuation`.

category_slug.description: Path segment of a category or make listing page, as in the site's URLs: `Excavators`, `Bobcat`, `Truck+Tractors`, `Skid+Steer+Loaders`, `Cat-Excavators`. Spaces are accepted and encoded as `+`. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 +._&',()-]*$.

continuation.description: Continuation cursor: the `next_offset` of the previous page as a decimal string. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,7}$.

include_facets.description: Also return the page's facet links (type, buying format, make, location, year, price, marketplace) with counts.

ironclad_assurance.description: Only items with (true) or without (false) IronClad Assurance (`ica`).

location.description: Location code (`l2`): a country (`USA`, `CAN`, `MEX`) or country-region (`USA-TX`). Pattern: ^[A-Z]{2,3}(-[A-Z0-9]{2,3})?$.

marketplace.description:
Marketplace (`ms`): I IronPlanet, M Marketplace-E, T TruckPlanet, G GovPlanet, R Ritchie Bros. Auctioneers, S SalvageSale.

Provider reference: allowed values ["I", "M", "T", "G", "R", "S"].

page_size.description:
Items per page (`prows`).

Provider reference: allowed values ["20", "60", "100"]; default 20.

price_bucket.description:
USD price bucket lower bound (`p_us`): -1 any USD price, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000, 100000, 500000, 1000000.

Provider reference: minimum -1.

sale_format.description:
Buying format (`fp`): D any auction, A online auction, L on-site auction, S sealed auction, B Buy Now, M Make Offer.

Provider reference: allowed values ["D", "A", "L", "S", "B", "M"].

sort.description:
Sort key as the site encodes it: `bm asc` Best Match, `p asc`/`p desc` price, `d asc` closest to the exit IP (not reproducible), `ad asc`/`ad desc` ending sooner/later, `yr desc` year (newest first).

Provider reference: allowed values ["bm asc", "p asc", "p desc", "d asc", "ad asc", "ad desc", "yr desc"]; default "bm asc".

type_id.description:

value.description: Unsere Durchgangskugelhähne aus Messing vernickelt sind als Muffen-Kugelhähne (Innengewinde), Einschraub-Kugelhähne (Innen-/Außengewinde) oder Kugelhähne mit beiderseits Außengewinde lieferbar. Die Kugelhähne sind mit Zulassungen wie zum Beispiel EN 331, DVGW, KTW (Trinkwasser) und natürlich auch in genormter Baulänge nach DIN 3202-M3 verfügbar. Sie können mit Standardgriff (auch abschließbar), Knebelgriff oder mit Federrückstellung betätigt werden. Durch das von uns eingeführte Kombigriff-System können Sie bei den meisten Kugelhähnen eine Vielzahl optionaler Griffe montieren. Tipp: Verwenden Sie, wo immer es möglich ist, Kugelhähne mit genormter Baulänge nach DIN 3202-M3. Bei einem späteren Austausch sparen Sie Anpassungen an dem Leitungsnetz.

value.body_text:
Key Points

It's been 10 years since Berkshire Hathaway first invested in Apple stock.

It has been the company's largest holding since 2017.

The Apple position encompasses many of Buffett's investing tenets.

10 stocks we like better than Apple ›(function(){ var m=document.getElementById("pit-c897e6a6-2dcd-4f50-aa4f-aee0c6c63ef8"); if(!m||!window.IntersectionObserver)return; var c=m;while(c&&!c.dataset.pitchPlacement)c=c.parentElement; if(!c)return; var fired=false; new IntersectionObserver(function(es,obs){ if(fired||!es[0].isIntersecting)return; fired=true;obs.disconnect(); new Image().src="https://api.fool.com/infotron/infotrack/seen/?impression=c897e6a6-2dcd-4f50-aa4f-aee0c6c63ef8&pitch_id=17995&placement=keypoints_pitch_feed_partner"; },{threshold:0.5}).observe(c); })();

Of all the great investments that former Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB) CEO Warren Buffett made over the years, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) might have been his best.

Up until his first investment in Apple in 2016, or perhaps with a position he opened in International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) in 2011, Buffett had been reluctant to invest in technology stocks because he said he didn't fully understand them.

Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But he soon understood Apple enough to make it his largest holding and best investment. Over the years, Berkshire has made more than $100 billion on Apple stock, Buffett told CNBC back in July of this year.

Former Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Best business in the world

Back in 2020 on CNBC, Buffett called Apple "probably the best business I know in the world," adding that he doesn't think of Apple as a stock. "I think of it as our third business." That would be a third business along with insurance and railroads.

That first investment in Apple stock was 9.8 million shares in the first quarter of 2016, when the stock traded at about $25 per share. It was just the beginning of Berkshire Hathaway's commitment to Apple, which Buffett himself discussed at the 2026 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder meeting back in May.

"About 10 years ago, we made a commitment to essentially move 10% of the total resources of Berkshire Hathaway. We turned it over to another person who was not that well known at the time, and we did that by spending roughly $35 billion buying stock in Apple Corp," Buffett said. "I would like to report that 10 years later, several things have happened. One is that the $35 billion -- counting dividends, realized appreciation, and unrealized appreciation -- has turned into $185 billion pretax."

Apple became Berkshire's largest holding by the end of 2017, representing about 15% of the total portfolio. Six years later, by the end of 2023, Berkshire had amassed a $174 billion investment in Apple, which made up a staggering 50% of its $347 billion portfolio.

After that, Buffett began paring back Berkshire Hathaway's Apple position. Part of it was surely profit-taking, but he also said in a recent interview that he was wary about having one stock take up 50% of the portfolio. Apple is still Berkshire's largest position, but it's "only" a $66 billion investment, making up 22% of the total portfolio.

The perfect Buffett investment

There are key takeaways from Berkshire's long-term commitment to Apple that illuminate some of Buffett's investing tenets. One is to buy great businesses at fair prices. In early 2016, Apple stock had slumped and was trading at a deep discount, at just 10 times earnings, its lowest valuation in 10 years.

It also represents Buffett's belief in investing in companies with strong leadership and management -- in this case, former Apple CEO Tim Cook. "When we made our investment and turned over 10% of Berkshire's resources, we were turning it over to Tim. As I say, he has turned that into $185 billion pretax," Buffett said at the shareholder meeting. "I think it's appropriate if Tim Cook would take a bow and our shareholders would say thanks to him."

Further, Apple had, and has, the kind of industry leadership and competitive moat that sets it up for long-term success. And of course, the 10-plus year investment in Apple shows the value of holding on to a great investment for the long term, even though Buffett himself recently admitted that he might have sold too soon on Apple.

But overall, Berkshire's investment in Apple isn't just a great example of the benefits of long-term investing. It also represents, perhaps, the perfect Buffett investment -- the culmination of everything he looks for in a stock.

200.description:
Nasdaq's RSS feed (`/feed/rssoutbound`) for one ticker, one topic category, or the whole site: the 15 newest articles, each with its exact publish instant (`published_at`, RFC 3339 UTC from pubDate, cross-checked against the guid epoch), publisher, topic, tagged tickers and teaser. This is the only Nasdaq list surface that carries a time of day. It lists articles only, never press releases. An unknown ticker or category is `not_found` (Nasdaq would silently answer the site-wide feed; that fallback is detected).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `items` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string |  |
| `kind` | string |  |
| `published_at` | string | pubDate, RFC 3339 UTC. |
| `published_at_epoch` | number | Unix seconds from the guid `?time=` parameter; equals `published_at`. |
| `publisher` | string | dc:creator; null when absent. |
| `tickers` | string[] | nasdaq:tickers, upper-cased, de-duplicated, Nasdaq's order. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `topic` | string | RSS category; null when absent. |

200.description:
Nasdaq.com's market-wide latest-news feed (`latestnews`), newest first across every syndicated publisher, up to 500 rows deep. Rows carry Nasdaq's calendar day and `ago` label plus `published_at` (RFC 3339 UTC) for the stories the default RSS feed lists (its 15 newest).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `items` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ago` | string | Nasdaq's relative label (`55 minutes ago`, `7 days ago`, or a date for older items) computed on Nasdaq's server at fetch time. It is a different clock from `published_date` and is not a publish time; see `observed_at_ms` for when it was read. |
| `description` | string | Teaser text; null when empty. |
| `id` | string | Nasdaq CMS node id; stable per story. |
| `image_url` | string |  |
| `kind` | string | From the URL family: /articles/, /press-release/, /videos/. |
| `primary_symbol` | string | Nasdaq's `primarysymbol`, upper-cased. Nasdaq fills it only for stories it files under one company; empty for most syndicated market wraps. |
| `primary_topic` | string | Topic name from `primarytopic` (Markets, Stocks, Technology...). |
| `primary_topic_id` | string | Topic term id from `primarytopic`; input for `topic_news`. |
| `published_at` | string | Publish instant, RFC 3339 UTC, taken from the matching Nasdaq RSS feed item (pubDate) when this story is among that feed's 15 newest items. Null otherwise; `article` returns the instant for any story. |
| `published_at_source` | string | `rss` when `published_at` came from the RSS feed; null when `published_at` is null. |
| `published_date` | string | Calendar day from Nasdaq's `created` field (US-Eastern day; the feed carries no time of day). Null when Nasdaq sends none. |
| `published_label` | string | Nasdaq's `created` text verbatim, e.g. `Sep 21, 2026`. |
| `publisher` | string | Syndication source as Nasdaq labels it (Zacks, The Motley Fool, Barchart, RTTNews...). Null when Nasdaq sends an empty string (most press releases). |
| `related_symbols` | object[] | Every symbol Nasdaq tagged on the story, upper-cased, in Nasdaq's order. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `url` | string | Absolute www.nasdaq.com URL of the story; pass it to `article` for the full text and the exact publish time. |

Rows carry Nasdaq's calendar day and `ago` label; the feed has no time of day and the ticker RSS feed lists no releases, so `published_at` is null on every row: pass the `url` to `article`, which reads the release page's `Published` stamp. A ticker with no releases returns zero rows; an unknown ticker is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `items` as the primary payload key.

| `description` | string | Teaser text; null when empty. |
| `id` | string | Nasdaq CMS node id; stable per story. |
| `image_url` | string |  |
| `kind` | string | From the URL family: /articles/, /press-release/, /videos/. |
| `mentions_ticker` | boolean | True when the requested ticker is among `related_symbols` or equals `primary_symbol`. Rows where this is false came from Nasdaq's market-wide fallback, not from the ticker's coverage. |

| `related_symbols` | object[] | Every symbol Nasdaq tagged on the story, upper-cased, in Nasdaq's order. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `url` | string | Absolute www.nasdaq.com URL of the story; pass it to `article` for the full text and the exact publish time. |

post.description: Third-party coverage of one stock or ETF, optionally for a date window: what moved a stock on a day (from/to with include_press_releases), recent coverage, or every story tagging the ticker (relevant_only: false). Official company announcements (deals, partnerships, earnings, launches) are press releases, which this feed omits: pass include_press_releases: true or call press_releases. For the exact publish time of any row pass its url to article; for only the 15 newest with times in one request use feed.

asset_class.description:
Nasdaq asset class of the ticker. `etf` for exchange-traded funds (SPY, QQQ); everything else is `stocks`.

Provider reference: allowed values ["stocks", "etf"]; default "stocks".

from.description: Earliest publish day to return, YYYY-MM-DD (US-Eastern, inclusive, compared with published_date). The scan stops at the first older story. Nasdaq keeps 500 rows per ticker, about two months for a heavily covered stock; a window_reached warning says when from lies beyond them. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

include_press_releases.description: Also fetch the ticker's `press_release` feed (one extra request) and merge its newest `limit` releases that pass `from`/`to` and `relevant_only` into the first page (`offset` 0) as `kind: press_release` rows, ordered newest first with the news by `published_date`; `count` may then exceed `limit`. Deeper pages are news only; `has_more` and `next_offset` follow the news feed. Releases carry no `published_at` (pass their `url` to `article` for it). For every release use `press_releases`.

limit.description:
Rows per page (1-100).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

offset.description:
Feed rows to skip, counting rows the filters skip too. Nasdaq serves at most 500 rows per feed and its edge denies deeper offsets, so 490 is the last usable offset; next_offset from the previous page is the safe value.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 490.

relevant_only.description: Return only stories about the ticker (about_ticker true): Nasdaq's primary_symbol is the ticker, or with no primary symbol the ticker is the only tag or the headline names the ticker or the company. false returns every story that tags the ticker, market wraps and stories filed under other companies included.

ticker.description: Exchange ticker as Nasdaq spells it (AAPL, BRK.B, SPY). Case-insensitive. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.\-]{0,9}$.

to.description: Latest publish day to return, YYYY-MM-DD (US-Eastern, inclusive). Newer stories are skipped. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

with_publish_times.description: Also fetch the matching RSS feed (one extra request) and copy its pubDate into `published_at` for the stories it lists (the 15 newest). Set false to save the request.

limit.description:
Rows per page (1-100).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

offset.description:
Rows to skip. Nasdaq serves at most 500 rows per feed and its edge denies deeper offsets, so 490 is the last usable offset; `next_offset` from the previous page is the safe value.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 490.

topic_id.description: Nasdaq topic term id, e.g. `4006` for Markets; read it from `primary_topic_id` on a feed row. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

with_publish_times.description: Also fetch the matching RSS feed (one extra request) and copy its pubDate into `published_at` for the stories it lists (the 15 newest). Set false to save the request.

200.description:
News stories under one Nasdaq topic (its `article?q=field_primary_topic:{id}` feed), newest first, up to 500 rows deep. Topic ids come from `primary_topic_id` on any feed row: 4006 Markets, 4301 Stocks, 4001 Technology, 4056 Investing. Rows carry `published_at` (RFC 3339 UTC) for the stories the topic's RSS feed lists (its 15 newest). An id Nasdaq has no rows for is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `items` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ago` | string | Nasdaq's relative label (`55 minutes ago`, `7 days ago`, or a date for older items) computed on Nasdaq's server at fetch time. It is a different clock from `published_date` and is not a publish time; see `observed_at_ms` for when it was read. |
| `description` | string | Teaser text; null when empty. |
| `id` | string | Nasdaq CMS node id; stable per story. |
| `image_url` | string |  |
| `kind` | string | From the URL family: /articles/, /press-release/, /videos/. |
| `primary_symbol` | string | Nasdaq's `primarysymbol`, upper-cased. Nasdaq fills it only for stories it files under one company; empty for most syndicated market wraps. |
| `primary_topic` | string | Topic name from `primarytopic` (Markets, Stocks, Technology...). |
| `primary_topic_id` | string | Topic term id from `primarytopic`; input for `topic_news`. |
| `published_at` | string | Publish instant, RFC 3339 UTC, taken from the matching Nasdaq RSS feed item (pubDate) when this story is among that feed's 15 newest items. Null otherwise; `article` returns the instant for any story. |
| `published_at_source` | string | `rss` when `published_at` came from the RSS feed; null when `published_at` is null. |
| `published_date` | string | Calendar day from Nasdaq's `created` field (US-Eastern day; the feed carries no time of day). Null when Nasdaq sends none. |
| `published_label` | string | Nasdaq's `created` text verbatim, e.g. `Sep 21, 2026`. |
| `publisher` | string | Syndication source as Nasdaq labels it (Zacks, The Motley Fool, Barchart, RTTNews...). Null when Nasdaq sends an empty string (most press releases). |
| `related_symbols` | object[] | Every symbol Nasdaq tagged on the story, upper-cased, in Nasdaq's order. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `url` | string | Absolute www.nasdaq.com URL of the story; pass it to `article` for the full text and the exact publish time. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Decode a VIN through NHTSA's recalls-site VIN lookup: vPIC decode (year, make, model, vehicle type) plus the matching NHTSA vehicle records (one per trim/series) with recall, complaint, investigation and manufacturer-communication counts. Model-level only: NHTSA's VIN-specific unrepaired-recall check (vinLookupWeb) sits behind reCAPTCHA Enterprise and is not exposed, so a vehicle with recall counts here may or may not have open recalls on this exact VIN.

The response contains the tool result directly.

results.caption:
Out of the box Claude can talk about a website but it can’t open one. These five change what it can physically do.
 
Playwright hands it a real browser, so it fills in the form, clicks through the page, and uses any site that never built a proper way in. Blotato connects it to your social accounts, so it posts for you, chops one video into a week of content, and builds the graphic itself.
 
Perplexity gives it live research, so instead of guessing from memory it reads the internet right now and shows you where every claim came from. Higgsfield opens the best video and image models up inside the chat. And Firecrawl reads any website end to end and pulls it back as clean text.
 
Ten minutes and it stops being a chatbot.
 
Comment SOCKET and I’ll send you the setup for all five.
 
#claudeai #mcp #aitools #claudecode #aiautomation

post.description: Search Oriane's indexed Instagram posts, captions and engagement. Platform is fixed to Instagram. Coverage and freshness depend on the existing index; this is not a complete live feed. Results include profileUrl; an empty result does not trigger ingestion. Choose projection: basic 35 credits, default 50 credits, full 65 credits per nonempty call. Search limit is at most 100; URL lookup targets one record. Empty results cost zero.

handle.description: Account username to match exactly, for example mrbeast. A leading @ is optional; usernames are matched without regard to case. Provide this or another search field; multiple fields must all match.

caption.description: Text to match in the caption. Provide this or another search field; multiple fields must all match.

limit.description:
Maximum results, default 20.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100.

offset.description:
Result offset, default 0.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

sort.description: Comma-separated sort fields with optional :asc or :desc. Profiles: followersCount, createdAt, updatedAt. Posts: viewsCount, likesCount, sharesCount, commentsCount, interactionsCount, engagementRatePerViews, engagementRatePerFollowers, profileFollowersCount, publishedAt, visualSimilarity, transcriptRelevance.

aiSearchAnchor.description: Anchor from the first visual search page, required for subsequent pages.

projection.description:
Response detail and fixed price per nonempty call: basic 35 credits, default 50 credits, full 65 credits. Empty results cost zero. Result limit does not change the tier price.

Provider reference: allowed values ["basic", "default", "full"]; default "default".

results.caption:
Out of the box Claude can talk about a website but it can’t open one. These five change what it can physically do.
 
Playwright hands it a real browser, so it fills in the form, clicks through the page, and uses any site that never built a proper way in. Blotato connects it to your social accounts, so it posts for you, chops one video into a week of content, and builds the graphic itself.
 
Perplexity gives it live research, so instead of guessing from memory it reads the internet right now and shows you where every claim came from. Higgsfield opens the best video and image models up inside the chat. And Firecrawl reads any website end to end and pulls it back as clean text.
 
Ten minutes and it stops being a chatbot.
 
Comment SOCKET and I’ll send you the setup for all five.
 
#claudeai #mcp #aitools #claudecode #aiautomation

Comment "MCP" and I'll send you the prompt that installs all three.

Out of the box, Claude is working blind.

No web, no browser, no current docs.

Three MCPs fix all three gaps.

Firecrawl gives it the open internet.

Point it at a competitor. Pull the whole site.

Playwright hands it your actual browser.

So it clicks through the app it just built.

And it tests instead of assuming.

Context7 pulls the live docs.

No more guessing at an API that already changed.

Like hiring someone smart with no internet.

Then giving them a laptop.

Same model. Completely different output.

Install once. Use it forever.

#claudecode #mcp #firecrawl #playwright #context7

Skills 👇🏻:

Skill Claude 1 - Humanizer
Sabe quando um texto parece que foi um robô que escreveu? Essa skill conserta isso. Pega o texto da IA e deixa com jeito de gente de verdade falando.
Ninguém percebe que foi a IA que escreveu.

Skill Claude 2 - Firecrawl
Normalmente o Claude não consegue entrar nos sites pra ler. Essa skill abre essa porta: ele entra, lê a página inteira e te traz o que importa.
É como mandar alguém pesquisar tudo na internet por você.

Skill Claude 3 - Superpower
Em vez de fazer uma coisa de cada vez, o Claude vira um time.
Ele pensa no plano, faz o trabalho e ainda confere se ficou bom no final.
Como ter vários ajudantes trabalhando juntos pra você.

Skill Claude 4 - Skill Builder
Essa é a skill que cria outras skills. Ela te faz umas perguntas e monta uma ferramenta do jeitinho que você precisa.
Se você faz a mesma coisa toda semana, ela deixa no automático.

Skill Claude 5 - MCP Builder
Essa skill liga o Claude com os seus programas, tipo planilhas e ferramentas de trabalho. Ela monta a “ponte” entre eles.
Aí o Claude para de só conversar e começa a fazer as coisas por você.

Skill Claude 6 - Marketing Skills by Corey Haines
Aqui o Claude aprende os truques de um dos maiores especialistas em vender pela internet. Ele te ajuda a saber pra quem vender e como.
É estratégia pronta, não só um textinho.

✨ Não use o Claude como um chatbot!!!
Todas essas skills vão transformar o Claude num super-funcionário.

Agora comenta “60” que envio todos os +60 comandos secretos do Claude 👇🏻

Three free tools that do what Apify, Firecrawl and ScrapingBee charge you monthly for.
 
ScrapeGraph AI is the one almost nobody names. You give it a link and a sentence describing what you want off the page, and it hands back clean structured data. No code, no selectors.
 
Agent Reach gets into the places that lock you out, LinkedIn, Instagram, X and Reddit, with no paid keys. Scrapling fixes the thing that actually kills scraping projects, which is a site redesigning and breaking everything you built.
 
One rule before you start: stick to public business information and respect the site’s rules. Free tools do not make everything permitted, and that part is in the guide.
 
Comment SPIDER and I’ll send you the links.
 
#scraping #leadgeneration #aitools #opensource #automation

It’s completely changed the way I build apps.

Try it here! https://link.lovable.dev/5RgYUIi

biography.blurb: Based in Los Angeles, James Axon is a musically studied and deep-digging DJ known for introducing dance floors to new sounds and new music, equally often through cutting-edge new releases as through the forgotten and obscure gems of the past.
biography.content:
James Axon is a DJ, musician, and creator of the LA-based queer underground party Planet Love, as well as a resident on Dublab with his radio show Hearing Color. A lifelong pianist turned obsessive record collector, James Axon approaches DJing as an extension of musicianship. Before falling into house and techno, he spent years in bands and orchestral ensembles, a background that still shapes the way he thinks about rhythm, harmony, and structuring his sets compositionally. 

As a keyboardist and musician, he has collaborated with Seven Davis Jr. and Massimiliano Pagliara, and as a DJ has shared lineups with the likes of Octo Octa, Eris Drew,  Avalon Emerson,The Blessed Madonna, Derrick Carter, Paramida, Peach, Moxie, Alex Kassian, Zombies in Miami, Jennifer Loveless, Sally C, Tornado Wallace, Perel, Eli Escobar, Paurro, and more. 

His sets drift seamlessly between house, techno, italo, electro, disco, and breaks, guided by an expansive taste shaped by pioneering artists like Aphex Twin, Kraftwerk, Giorgio Moroder, Jeff Mills, Laurent Garnier, Andrew Weatherall, and Francois Kevorkian. His sets are always colorful, eclectic, and intuitively reflective of the setting -- whether playing cosmic disco in an intimate loft or hypnotic techno in a dark foggy warehouse, he still finds a sound that is distinctly James Axon: melodic and synth-heavy, driving and dreamy.

post.description: Discover events by city and date; take `area_id` from `areas` and chain each `events[].id` into `event` for tickets.

area_id.description:
RA area id from `areas` (8 New York City, 34 Berlin, 13 London, 1 Sydney). RA stores area ids as 16-bit integers.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 32767.

date_from.description: First local listing date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today (UTC). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

date_to.description: Last local listing date, inclusive. Default: `date_from` + 7 days; at most 366 days after `date_from`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

page.description:
1-based page; use `next_page` from the previous response.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200.

page_size.description:
Rows per page, default 20.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

query.description: Keyword matched against event titles within the area and window.

sort.description:
`date`: RA's listing order (listing date, then relevance score, then title). `popularity`: most attending first. Default `date`.

Provider reference: allowed values ["date", "popularity"].

value.cancellation_policy: Cancellations more than 48 hours in advance of arrival date only incur a $10 transaction fee.  Within 48 hours, $10 and the first night's fee are charged (Exception: 1 night reservations do not incur an additional $10 fee, but do not receive a refund).  No-shows will be assessed a $20 service fee along with the loss of the first night's fee.

descriptions.html: For facility specific information, please call (209) 372-8502.
descriptions.title: Contact Info

descriptions.html:
Upper Pines Campground is the largest of the three reservation campgrounds in Yosemite Valley. It offers paved roads and parking spurs, flush toilets, and drinking water. Each campsite contains a picnic table, fire ring, and a food storage locker.
Yosemite's free shuttle bus stops at the campground entrance. Nearby, historic Curry Village offers showers (for a fee), a general store, restaurants and bar, amphitheater and a tour and activities desk.
descriptions.title: Facilities

descriptions.html: Yosemite Valley is forested with a diverse mix of California black oak, Ponderosa pine, incense-cedar, White fir, and Whiteleaf Manzanita, which offers a pleasant combination of sun and shade. Through the trees, Yosemite's telltale granite cliffs peek through, and the gentle, refreshing Merced River flows nearby.
descriptions.title: Natural Features

descriptions.html:
Glacier Point offers sweeping views of Yosemite Valley, Little Yosemite Valley, Half Dome, Vernal and Nevada Falls, and Clouds Rest, among other notable landmarks.

The Tioga Road offers a 39-mile scenic drive past forests, meadows, lakes and granite domes. Beautiful Hetch Hetchy Reservoir is home to spectacular scenery and numerous wilderness trailheads.
descriptions.title: Nearby Attractions

descriptions.html:
Upper Pines campsites are available to reserve up to five months in advance on the 15th of each month at 7:00 a.m. PST. For example, on January 15, arrival dates for the period May 15 to June 14 become available to reserve, and therefore, the full arrival date window would be from January 15 to June 14. 

Reservation Tips! Campsites in Yosemite are extremely popular and typically sell out in minutes. Login to your account or create a new account before the 7:00 a.m. (PST) release time. You may only add reservations to your cart and proceed with your reservation if you are logged into your account. The recreation.gov call center does NOT have access to additional sites or additional information beyond what is published on recreation.gov. 

Upper Pines Campground is located in breathtaking Yosemite National Park in Central California's rugged Sierra Nevada Mountain Range at an elevation of 4,000 feet. The site is situated in the heart of Yosemite Valley, an awe-inspiring landscape containing many of the famous features for which Yosemite National Park is known. Within Yosemite, visitors can gaze upon waterfalls, sheer granite cliffs, deep valleys, grand meadows, ancient giant sequoias, vast wilderness areas and much more. 


Yosemite National Park Campground Reservation Dates 

For additional park information, call (209)372-0200 or visit www.nps.gov/yose
descriptions.title: Overview

descriptions.html:
Yosemite's trails, cliffs, roads and rivers provide endless recreational activities for any kind of visitor. Hiking, biking, rock climbing, fishing, horseback riding, rafting, auto touring, cross-country skiing and photography are all very popular activities within the park.

Hiking trails range from the easy paved, two-mile roundtrip walk to Mirror Lake/Meadow, to the grueling but rewarding 14- to 16-mile trek to Half Dome (permit required). Both of these trails begin near the Pines Campgrounds, and there are many additional trailheads within Yosemite Valley.

Rafting the Merced River is a fun way to cool down on a summer day when water levels are sufficient. Yosemite Valley also offers numerous guided bus tours, educational programs, museums, ranger-led activities and an art center with workshops.

notices.text: You are responsible for reading the site alerts and booking a site that will accommodate your equipment.
If arriving one or more days late, call (209) 372-8502; your reservation will be cancelled if we do not hear from you within 24 hours of your arrival date.
You must check-in at the campground kiosk upon arrival. After-hours arrivals must sign-in and return to the kiosk to complete check-in the following morning or your reservation may be cancelled.

Bears and other wildlife live here! Food and toiletries must be properly stored 24 hours/day.  

  • Food storage lockers are provided in all campsites (35 inches deep x 43 inches wide x 28 inches high). 

  • Absolutely no food stored in vehicles. 

  • Dispose of garbage immediately in bear-proof dumpsters.
There are no electric, water or sewer hook-ups available at individual campsites. A free dump station is located on-site along with potable water.
Your camping reservation does NOT get you into Yosemite for free. You must pay an additional fee per vehicle at the park entrance or buy a pass ahead of time on recreation.gov.

Road conditions can change at any time; before arrival, please call (209) 372-0200 for road and weather conditions inside Yosemite, and 1-800-427-ROAD for conditions outside the park. For additional park information, call (209) 372-0200 or visit www.nps.gov/yose

Don't Move Firewood: Help protect our forests! Prevent the spread of tree-killing pests by obtaining firewood at or near your destination and burning it on-site. Moving firewood is illegal in some states. Visit dontmovefirewood.org to learn more.

Help Yosemite be a Zero Landfill park! Leave excess packaging at home. Use refillable propane bottles, water bottles, food containers and travel mugs. Place all of your recyclable waste in designated recycling containers. For more information go to: https://www.nps.gov/yose/getinvolved/zlf.htm
Resale or auction of advance reservations is prohibited.

reviews.review: Beautiful campsite! Did not have neighbors for most of our stay, and then bathrooms were very clean. There is also a drinking water station and a water waste disposal station. As others said, you are close to the dumpsters but I didn’t think it was a big problem or noisy. Would definitely stay here again (:

We were in site 1 which has some pros and cons. The pros are no neighbors on one side and the camp hosts are really friendly. The cons are instead of neighbors you have dumpsters. That said, it doesn't matter because you are out seeing the valley all day not hanging in camp and the valley is AWESOME.
